{{Quote|And did you complete the Padawan birthday ritual? Only by remembering the past are we able to learn from the present.|Master Qui-Gon Jinn, to his Padawan, Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="JA3" />}}
The '''Padawan birthday ritual''' was a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] tradition in the last [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Taking place on a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan's]] thirteenth [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]], the apprentice would reflect on the past and receive a special gift from [[Gender/Legends|their]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]]. In [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], Padawan [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] took part in the ritual; the young apprentice failed to find the [[Time/Legends|time]] for the reflection portion and was initially dismayed by [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|his Master's]] choice of what appeared to be a [[River stone|simple rock]] as a gift, but he later came to value the stone after he learned that it was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]]. [[29 BBY/Legends|Fifteen years later]], Kenobi's own apprentice, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], would take part; Kenobi regifted the stone to his Padawan, who immediately appreciated it.

==Description==
{{Quote|Are you sure? This was given to you by Qui-Gon.''"<br />"''He would want you to have it, as I do. It is my most treasured possession. I hope it will be with you always to remind you of Qui-Gon and me, of our deep regard for you.''"<br />"''I'll treasure it. Thank you, Master.|Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="JQ1">''[[Jedi Quest: The Way of the Apprentice]]''</ref>}}
The [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]] ritual was a tradition observed by members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the later [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the reign of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Practiced by Padawans on their thirteenth birthday, the ritual entailed quiet reflection on their past, [[Meditation/Legends|meditating]] on positive memories as well as bad ones, in lieu of a birthday celebration. According to [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], one needed to reflect on past events to learn from current ones. Additionally, the Padawan would receive a gift from their Master, who often considered the gift for several [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] or even [[Standard month/Legends|months]] and sometimes traveled long distances to obtain it. Example gifts included [[healing crystal]]s, cloaks from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pasmin]] known for their seeming lack of weight,<ref name="JA3" /> or special [[Lightsaber hilt/Legends|lightsaber hilts]].<ref name="JQ1" />

==History==
{{Quote|I'm glad of one thing, Padawan. You have held on to your memories.''"<br />"''Your river stone helped me. I did not realize the stone was Force-sensitive. I should have known you would have given me something of great value.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="JA3" />}}
In [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> following the completion of a [[Mission to Bandomeer|mission]] to the planet [[Bandomeer/Legends|Bandomeer]], Padawan [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was unable to find time to complete the reflection portion of the ritual. His Master, Jinn, nearly forgot about Kenobi's birthday and gave his apprentice a [[river stone]] taken from the [[River of Light]] on [[Qui-Gon Jinn's homeworld|Jinn's home planet]] before gently chiding him about his failure to complete the ritual. Kenobi was disappointed in the choice of gift, feeling that the trust that he thought he had received from Jinn on the previous mission was not there. However, during the [[Revolution on Phindar|next mission]] on the planet [[Phindar/Legends|Phindar]], Kenobi was captured by the [[Syndicat]], the ruling criminal organization, and sentenced to have all of his [[Renewal|memories erased]]. While awaiting the carrying out of this sentence, Kenobi began to regret not completing the reflection and meditation exercise, but then he discovered that the [[Force-sensitive stone|stone]] he had been given was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] and was able to use the power of the [[Stone/Legends|stone]] to resist the mind wipe. After the mission, he appreciated the gift much more for that quality,<ref name="JA3" /> and it would eventually become his most valued possession, so much so that his friend [[Bant Eerin/Legends|Bant Eerin]] sewed a pocket in his tunic for him so that he could hold it near his [[Heart/Legends|heart]].<ref name="JQ1" />

Kenobi eventually gained [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knighthood]] himself and took [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] as a Padawan.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> [[29 BBY/Legends|Fifteen years after]]<ref name="29 BBY">According to [[Leland Chee]] ({{Blog|holocron|13/comments|Major Character Birth Years}}), Anakin Skywalker's birth year is 41.9 BBY; therefore, his thirteenth birthday can be placed at 28.9 BBY.</ref> receiving the river stone from Jinn, on the [[Standard day/Legends|day]] that Skywalker turned thirteen, Kenobi passed the rock on to his own apprentice, knowing that his former Master would want him to pass it on. Skywalker was much more appreciative of the present than Kenobi originally had been, as he knew that it had originally come from Jinn,<ref name="JQ1" /> who had rescued him from [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] and brought him to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] to be [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] [[32 BBY/Legends|three years earlier]] but [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|died]] before he could begin Skywalker's training himself.<ref name="TPM" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Padawan birthday ritual first appeared in [[Jedi Apprentice: The Hidden Past|''The Hidden Past'']], the [[1999]] third book in [[Jude Watson]]'s young readers [[Star Wars: Jedi Apprentice|''Jedi Apprentice'']] series.<ref name="JA3" />
